sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Parents, at least of a certain era, used to tell their kids,
sentences.zh: 父母们，至少在某个时代，过去常常告诉他们的孩子，

sentences.en: if you can't say anything nice, don't say anything at all.
sentences.zh: 如果你说不出什么好听的话，那就什么也别说。

sentences.en: Such advice might seem quaint today.
sentences.zh: 这样的忠告在今天看来或许有些过时。

sentences.en: No matter where we look, it can feel as if we're living in a time of mounting incivility.
sentences.zh: 无论我们看向哪里，似乎都置身于一个粗鲁无礼日益滋生的时代。

sentences.en: Smartphones and social media amplify this feeling.
sentences.zh: 智能手机和社交媒体放大了这种感觉。

sentences.en: It used to be that when two people got into an argument in a parking lot
sentences.zh: 过去，当两个人在停车场

sentences.en: or on an airplane, only a few people heard it.
sentences.zh: 或飞机上争吵时，只有少数人能听到。

sentences.en: But today, thousands of people witness rude interactions among people they'll never meet.
sentences.zh: 但如今，成千上万的人目睹了他们素不相识的人之间的粗鲁互动。

sentences.en: It's become the stuff of viral videos and memes.
sentences.zh: 这已经成了疯传视频和网络表情包的素材。

sentences.en: We're not talking to you.
sentences.zh: 我们又不是在跟你说话。

sentences.en: Yeah, but we're not talking to you.
sentences.zh: 对啊，但我们又不是在跟你说话。

sentences.en: Why don't you mind your own business?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不多管管自己的闲事？

sentences.en: Because we're not talking to you.
sentences.zh: 因为我们没在跟你说话。

sentences.en: We're not one of these people that work here, so get out of my face.
sentences.zh: 我们又不是在这工作的，少在我面前晃悠。

sentences.en: We often tell ourselves to ignore insults and slights.
sentences.zh: 我们常常告诉自己要忽视侮辱和轻视。

sentences.en: Yet psychological experiments show that this is not easy to do
sentences.zh: 然而心理学实验表明，这并不容易做到，

sentences.en: and that rudeness has a long-lasting, malevolent power.
sentences.zh: 而且无礼具有持久而恶劣的力量。

sentences.en: We're flooded with emotions, and that's when this fight-or-flight gear kicks in.
sentences.zh: 我们被情绪淹没，这时候战或逃的本能机制就开始启动了。

sentences.en: You know, one way that I think about this is like the storm inside your brain.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我思考这个问题的一个方式，就像是你大脑内部的风暴。

sentences.en: The surprising effects of incivility
sentences.zh: 无礼的惊人影响

sentences.en: and how to protect yourself from its toxic influence.
sentences.zh: 以及如何保护自己免受其毒害。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Rudeness and incivility seem to be showing up everywhere these days.
sentences.zh: 粗鲁和无礼如今似乎随处可见。

sentences.en: On airplanes, in supermarket aisles, in restaurants.
sentences.zh: 在飞机上、超市过道里、餐馆里。

sentences.en: What effect does this tide of nastiness have on all of us?
sentences.zh: 这股恶劣的风气对我们所有人都产生了什么影响？

sentences.en: According to the old adage,
sentences.zh: 根据这句老话，

sentences.en: sticks and stones may break my bones, but words will never hurt me.
sentences.zh: 恶语伤人六月寒（原意：棍棒石头可能会打断我的骨头，但言语永远伤害不到我）。

sentences.en: But is this really true?
sentences.zh: 但这真的是真的吗？

sentences.en: At Georgetown University, behavioral scientist Christine Porath
sentences.zh: 在乔治城大学，行为科学家克里斯蒂娜·波拉思

sentences.en: studies the effects of incivility on our communities, our careers,
sentences.zh: 研究了无礼对我们的社区、我们的职业，

sentences.en: even our capacity for creativity.
sentences.zh: 甚至对我们的创造力的影响。

sentences.en: Christine Porath, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·波拉思，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: I want to start by having you tell me about a moment in your own life, Christine,
sentences.zh: 我想先请你讲讲你生活中的一个时刻，克里斯蒂娜，

sentences.en: where you saw the effects of incivility firsthand.
sentences.zh: 在那时你亲眼目睹了无礼的影响。

sentences.en: You were still a student in college when you received word
sentences.zh: 你当时还在读大学，突然接到消息

sentences.en: that your dad was in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 说你父亲住院了。

sentences.en: Can you describe the scene for me when you got there?
sentences.zh: 当你到达那里时，能为我描述一下当时的场景吗？

sentences.en: Well, I remember vividly walking up to the hospital room
sentences.zh: 嗯，我清晰地记得自己走向病房，

sentences.en: and being in the doorway and seeing him lying there in the hospital bed
sentences.zh: 站在门口，看到他躺在病床上，

sentences.en: with electrodes strapped to his bare cheSt.
sentences.zh: 赤裸的胸膛上绑着电极。

sentences.en: And it was shocking for me to see him like that
sentences.zh: 看到他那个样子让我感到震惊，

sentences.en: because he was an otherwise, you know, very strong, vivacious, athletic guy.
sentences.zh: 因为在我的印象中，他一直是个非常强壮、充满活力、热爱运动的人。

sentences.en: And I had never envisioned something like that happening to him.
sentences.zh: 我从未想过这种事会发生在他身上。

sentences.en: Why was he in the hospital?
sentences.zh: 他为什么会住院？

sentences.en: Well, he had had a heart attack and this stemmed from working for a very toxic boss.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他心脏病发作了，而这源于他在一个非常刻薄的老板手下工作。

sentences.en: He had actually worked for two toxic bosses for over the course of a decade.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在十多年的时间里，他一直在两个刻薄的老板手下工作。

sentences.en: And it was, you know, really coming to a breaking point.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那真的是到了崩溃的边缘。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until I thought a decade later or more
sentences.zh: 直到我想大约十年或更久之后，

sentences.en: that he shared some of the particulars and really spoke openly about that.
sentences.zh: 他才分享了一些细节，并真正公开谈论了这件事。

sentences.en: And the truth was it was painful for him to relive that stuff.
sentences.zh: 事实是，重温那些经历对他来说很痛苦。

sentences.en: Christine's father was a salesman.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜的父亲是一名推销员。

sentences.en: His boss would insult staff members in meetings and blame them for things beyond their control.
sentences.zh: 他的老板经常在会议上侮辱员工，把超出他们控制范围的事情归咎于他们。

sentences.en: He even belittled clients.
sentences.zh: 他甚至贬低客户。

sentences.en: During a visit to a client store, my dad heard his boss tell the owner,
sentences.zh: 在拜访客户店铺期间，我父亲听到老板对店主说：

sentences.en: I see you're carrying on your father's tradition.
sentences.zh: 我看得出你在继承你父亲的传统。

sentences.en: The store looked like s**t then and it looks like s**t in your hands.
sentences.zh: 这家店当时看起来像狗屎，落到你手里看起来还是像狗屎。

sentences.en: The idea of people being put on the spot was something in a meeting.
sentences.zh: 把人当场架在火上烤的想法在会议上时有发生。

sentences.en: You know, you don't know what you're doing here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在这里根本不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Screaming certainly took place, which I would say like crosses the line of what I tend to study.
sentences.zh: 当然也发生过大喊大叫，我认为这已经超越了我所研究的底线。

sentences.en: So some years later, you were working at your first job.
sentences.zh: 所以几年后，你开始从事你的第一份工作。

sentences.en: It was at a sports academy in Florida.
sentences.zh: 那是在佛罗里达州的一个体育学院。

sentences.en: And an incident took place early one morning before work at the company gym.
sentences.zh: 一天清晨上班前，在公司的健身房里发生了一起事件。

sentences.en: Can you paint me a picture of what happened, Christine?
sentences.zh: 你能为我描绘一下当时发生了什么吗，克里斯蒂娜？

sentences.en: My friend who ran the Performance Institute, he would open it up early for us to work out before the gym was open to athletes.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友经营着那个运动表现研究所，他会很早为我们开门，好让我们在健身房对运动员开放前锻炼。

sentences.en: And, you know, he would have music playing in the background, kind of energetic workout music.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他会放背景音乐，那种充满活力的健身音乐。

sentences.en: And we'd all be doing our thing on the treadmills and somewhere lifting weights.
sentences.zh: 我们都在跑步机上做着自己的事，有些人则在举重。

sentences.en: And ironically, the person whose name was on the sports agency showed up.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，这家体育机构冠名本尊的人出现了。

sentences.en: And oftentimes he was out of town traveling the world.
sentences.zh: 而他通常都不在城里，四处旅行。

sentences.en: So this was unexpected.
sentences.zh: 所以这是意料之外的。

sentences.en: And he just started screaming at the performance manager, you know, saying,
sentences.zh: 他开始冲着表现经理大喊大叫，你知道的，说道：

sentences.en: you know that I love Barry White.
sentences.zh: 你知道我最喜欢巴里·怀特。

sentences.en: Why isn't my music playing?
sentences.zh: 为什么不放我的音乐？

sentences.en: So, you know, my friend went in the back and changed the music to Barry White.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我的朋友走到后面把音乐换成了巴里·怀特。

sentences.en: And then we all kind of put our heads down and people's minds were swirling a little bit
sentences.zh: 然后我们大家都有点把头埋低，大家的脑子里都在胡思乱想，

sentences.en: in terms of what they had just witnessed and why that happened
sentences.zh: 想着他们刚刚目睹了什么，为什么会发生这种事，

sentences.en: and what did that mean for them during the day.
sentences.zh: 以及这对他们当天的生活意味着什么。

sentences.en: But the biggest thing, I think, was just the way that it affected people's emotions and moods.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的事情，我认为，正是它对人们情绪和心情的影响。

sentences.en: And they weren't themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们不再是自己了。

sentences.en: Like they didn't bring the same energy to the athletes or the customers
sentences.zh: 就像他们没有把同样的精力带给运动员、客户，

sentences.en: or the people that they were dealing with that day.
sentences.zh: 或是他们那天要打交道的人。

sentences.en: I want to talk about one other story that reveals what it feels like to be directly on the receiving end of incivility.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈另一个故事，它揭示了亲身遭受无礼对待时的感受。

sentences.en: Some years after you left the sports academy in Florida, you became an academic.
sentences.zh: 在你离开佛罗里达的那家体育学院几年后，你成为了一名学者。

sentences.en: You were a junior professor at a school and you had an encounter with a senior professor at a holiday party.
sentences.zh: 你在某所学校担任初级教授，在一次节日派对上，你与一位资深教授发生了冲突。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what happened?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: We were talking just kind of over in the corner.
sentences.zh: 我们当时只是在角落里随便聊聊。

sentences.en: And he said that he thought my book had a stupid title.
sentences.zh: 他说他觉得我的书名很蠢。

sentences.en: And, you know, I didn't really know what to say in response to that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我当时真的不知道该作何回应。

sentences.en: I just kind of took it.
sentences.zh: 我只能默默承受。

sentences.en: But I really just wanted to escape the situation.
sentences.zh: 但我真的只想逃离那个处境。

sentences.en: And I certainly didn't ask for his opinion about the title.
sentences.zh: 我当然没有征求他对书名的意见。

sentences.en: So it really took me off track because I remember, you know, days afterwards kind of sitting in my office,
sentences.zh: 所以这真的把我打乱了阵脚，因为我记得，你知道的，几天后我坐在办公室里，

sentences.en: staring at the computer screen and just thinking about that and what it meant for the prospects of my career because I was up for tenure.
sentences.zh: 盯着电脑屏幕，脑子里一直在想这件事，以及它对我职业前景意味着什么，因为我当时正在争取终身教职。

sentences.en: And our profession, that means like you're up or out.
sentences.zh: 在我们的行业里，这意味着要么升职，要么走人。

sentences.en: You either have a job or you're going to lose that job and need to uproot yourself and your whole life from that place.
sentences.zh: 要么你保住工作，要么你就会失去工作，不得不连根拔起，带着你整个人生离开那个地方。

sentences.en: So, you know, I felt like I had a lot riding on it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我觉得自己押上了很多筹码。

sentences.en: And given that he had a lot of power and status and everything else, I just wondered what that meant for me and my future.
sentences.zh: 鉴于他拥有很大的权力和地位以及其他一切，我只是在想这对我和我的未来意味着什么。

sentences.en: I'm wondering how you behaved around the senior professor.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你在那位资深教授周围是如何表现的。

sentences.en: You must have bumped into him in the hallways or passed him at meetings or, you know,
sentences.zh: 你肯定在走廊里偶遇过他，或者在会议上擦肩而过，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: did it change your behavior and how you interacted with him going forward?
sentences.zh: 这有没有改变你的行为以及你日后与他互动的方式？

sentences.en: Yeah, it definitely changed my behavior.
sentences.zh: 是的，它确实改变了我的行为。

sentences.en: I really tried to avoid him and work with my office door closed.
sentences.zh: 我真的很极力躲着他，工作时办公室的门也关着。

sentences.en: I really almost like timed when I would go to the bathroom to avoid people.
sentences.zh: 我甚至几乎像算准时间一样去洗手间以避开人群。

sentences.en: I think that I kind of became a shell of myself around him and other people.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在面对他和别人的时候，我都快变成一具空壳了。

sentences.en: So that single moment of incivility stayed with you for a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以那个单次的不礼貌行为在你身上留存了很长时间。

sentences.en: And it makes me think about the long term effects of all the rudeness we see around us.
sentences.zh: 这让我联想到我们周围看到的种种无礼行为所带来的长期影响。

sentences.en: It does seem as though there has been an increase in incivility, perhaps as the COVID pandemic has worn us all down.
sentences.zh: 看起来无礼现象确实有所增加，也许是因为新冠大流行让我们所有人都感到身心俱疲。

sentences.en: In January 2022, a customer at a smoothie shop in Fairfield, Connecticut, received the wrong drink.
sentences.zh: 2022年1月，在康涅狄格州费尔菲尔德的一家奶昔店里，一名顾客拿错了饮料。

sentences.en: He claimed it contained peanut butter.
sentences.zh: 他声称里面含有花生酱。

sentences.en: And he said his son had had an allergic reaction and needed to be hospitalized.
sentences.zh: 并且他说他的儿子有过敏反应，需要住院治疗。

sentences.en: The man confronted two young employees at the smoothie shop, calling one of them an immigrant loser.
sentences.zh: 这名男子与奶昔店的两名年轻员工发生了对质，并称其中一人为移民失败者。

sentences.en: The exchange, which is really quite disturbing to hear, went viral on social media.
sentences.zh: 这段交流听起来实在令人不安，在社交媒体上广为流传。

sentences.en: Christine, it could be that we're hearing about incidents like this because of social media,
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜，我们听到这样的事件可能是因为社交媒体，

sentences.en: but it does feel like almost every other week brings a new example of people simply losing it.
sentences.zh: 但感觉几乎每隔一周就会有新的例子，显示人们彻底失控。

sentences.en: Do you think there is more incivility around us these days?
sentences.zh: 你认为如今我们身边的无礼现象更多了吗？

sentences.en: I do, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我确实这么认为。

sentences.en: And our and other research would suggest that the number one reason for incivility is that people feel stressed or overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 我们以及其他人的研究表明，无礼的首要原因是人们感到压力山大或不堪重负。

sentences.en: I think that, you know, unfortunately, that kind of negativity, even around, you know, the pandemic, around politics, around uncertainty,
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，不幸的是，这种负面情绪，甚至是围绕着大流行、政治、不确定性的负面情绪，

sentences.en: leads us to feel more stressed and is a reason that at least people say caused their rudeness or responding negatively in moments like those.
sentences.zh: 让我们感到压力更大，这也是人们至少承认导致自己粗鲁或在那种时刻做出负面反应的原因。

sentences.en: Healthcare systems in particular, it's just terrible these days.
sentences.zh: 特别是医疗系统，现在的情况真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And CEOs of hospitals, some of them have reached out to me and said, do you know how bad it is right now?
sentences.zh: 有些医院的首席执行官甚至联系过我，说：‘你知道现在情况有多糟糕吗？’

sentences.en: And I think, just like this clip alludes to, a lot of this is mixed with racism and politics.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，正如这段音频所暗示的那样，许多这样的事件都与种族主义和政治交织在一起。

sentences.en: So they are on the front lines of getting this, and it's just become really, really hard for them.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们正处于承受这一切的最前线，对他们来说，这一切已经变得非常非常艰难。

sentences.en: When we come back, the surprisingly powerful effects that incivility has on our brains and what we can do about it.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们将为您带来：无礼对我们大脑产生的惊人强大影响，以及我们该如何应对。

sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: If you recently had a stand in a long line at the airport or waited for a bus that never showed up
sentences.zh: 如果你最近在机场排过漫长的队伍，或者苦等一辆始终没来的公交车，

sentences.en: or had to deal with an incompetent customer service rep in a call center,
sentences.zh: 又或者不得不应付呼叫中心里不称职的客服代表，

sentences.en: you may have felt a rising level of impatience.
sentences.zh: 你可能会感到内心的不耐烦情绪不断上升。

sentences.en: It may have taken all your effort to keep your frustrations under control.
sentences.zh: 你可能需要耗费全部的精力才能控制住自己的挫败感。

sentences.en: Many of us can think of situations where we lost it or where we saw others lose their cool.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人都能想到自己情绪失控，或者看到别人失去冷静的场景。

sentences.en: Social media is full of videos showing people screaming at each other in stores, in restaurants,
sentences.zh: 社交媒体上到处都是视频，显示人们在商店、餐馆里大声尖叫，

sentences.en: and in workplaces.
sentences.zh: 以及在工作场所中。

sentences.en: At Georgetown University, behavioral scientist Christine Porath studies the effects of this tide of incivility.
sentences.zh: 在乔治城大学，行为科学家克里斯蒂娜·波拉思研究了这股无礼风气的影响。

sentences.en: Christine, when you were in high school, you played on a boys' soccer team.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜，你上高中时，曾在一个男生足球队踢球。

sentences.en: And I understand that at the time, you felt that the best way to deal with rudeness was just to shake it off?
sentences.zh: 据我了解，当时你觉得应对粗鲁的最好方法就是甩掉它，别放在心上？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I think just coming from that background, it's the idea that you should be strong and rise above it and just power through.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想正是由于那种背景，让你觉得你应该坚强，超越它，咬牙坚持过去。

sentences.zh: 当你目睹粗鲁行为时，你就会把它传递下去。

sentences.en: You know, Christine, we've seen YouTube and Twitter and Facebook are full of examples of
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在任何地方看到它——在线上、在媒体上，你很可能会成为

sentences.zh: 这种病毒的载体，并将它传递给你接触的任何人。

sentences.en: are basically spread far and wide on the internet.
sentences.zh: 其中很多都是无意识的。

sentences.en: But I think what you're saying is that there's a different kind of virality that rudeness and
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，有没有办法让覆水难收的局面重回正轨？

sentences.en: incivility can have.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's what we find in our research is both within the workplace as well as outside
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: of it.
sentences.zh: 行为科学家克里斯蒂娜·波拉特专门研究粗鲁无礼现象。

sentences.en: When you witness incivility, you pass it forward.
sentences.zh: 她发现这会对我们的思维、情绪和

sentences.en: And so if you're seeing it anywhere, online, on the media, you will likely become a carrier
sentences.zh: 福祉产生强大且持久的影响。

sentences.en: of this virus and pass it forward with whoever you come in contact with.
sentences.zh: 尽管很难获得关于此事的精确数据，但人们很难摆脱这样一种感觉，

sentences.en: And a lot of that is unintentional.
sentences.zh: 即粗鲁无礼的现象正在呈上升趋势。

sentences.zh: 我们对此能做些什么呢？

sentences.en: When people treat us rudely, our first impulse might be to respond in kind.
sentences.zh: 当人们粗鲁地对待我们时，我们的第一冲动可能是以牙还牙。

sentences.en: But Christine says it's a good idea to reflect that at least sometimes, rudeness can be
sentences.zh: 但克里斯蒂（Christine）认为，思考一下至少有时这种粗鲁可能是

sentences.en: unintentional.
sentences.zh: 无意的，这是一个好主意。

sentences.en: When we asked why people are rude, only 4% said because it's fun and they can get away
sentences.zh: 当我们询问人们为什么会表现得粗鲁时，只有4%的人说是因为好玩而且可以

sentences.en: with it.
sentences.zh: 逃脱惩罚。

sentences.en: I think the vast majority of people have no idea that what they're doing is hurting
sentences.zh: 我认为绝大多数人根本不知道他们的所作所为正在伤害

sentences.en: people or making them feel small in some way.
sentences.zh: 别人，或者在某种程度上让他们觉得自己很渺小。

sentences.en: And so I believe it stems from a lack of self-awareness.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信这源于自我觉察的缺乏。

sentences.en: In her work with groups and organizations, Christine sometimes draws on an old idea from
sentences.zh: 在与团队和组织的合作中，克里斯蒂有时会借鉴心理学上的一个老概念，

sentences.en: psychology, the Johari window.
sentences.zh: 即乔哈里视窗（Johari window）。

sentences.en: The psychologists Joseph Luft and Harrington Ingham divided a square into quadrants, like
sentences.zh: 心理学家约瑟夫·鲁夫特（Joseph Luft）和哈林顿·英格姆（Harrington Ingham）将一个正方形划分为四个象限，就像

sentences.en: a four-paned window.
sentences.zh: 一个四扇窗户的玻璃窗。

sentences.en: One pane represents things we know about ourselves that others know as well.
sentences.zh: 其中一扇窗代表我们自己知道、别人也知道的事情。

sentences.en: A second looks at secrets, things that we know about ourselves that others do not know.
sentences.zh: 第二扇窗关注的是秘密，也就是我们自己知道、而别人不知道的事情。

sentences.en: Another looks at elements of ourselves that are unknown both to us and to others.
sentences.zh: 另一扇窗关注的是我们身上连我们自己和别人都不知道的元素。

sentences.en: Christine focuses on a final pane.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂聚焦于最后一扇窗。

sentences.en: Things that others know about us that we don't know about ourselves.
sentences.zh: 也就是别人知道我们、而我们自己却不知道的事情。

sentences.en: The Johari window is really this idea of what we know about ourself, what we do not know about
sentences.zh: 乔哈里视窗实际上就是这样一种概念：关于我们自己知道什么、我们自己不知道什么、

sentences.en: ourself, what others know about us, and what others do not know about us.
sentences.zh: 别人对我们了解什么以及别人对我们不了解什么。

sentences.en: And so we're really trying to uncover our blind spots around what's known to others but is
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际上是在试图揭开我们的盲区，也就是那些别人知道但

sentences.en: not known to ourself because these blind spots are really what's affecting how we're behaving
sentences.zh: 我们自己不知道的事情，因为这些盲区才是真正影响我们行为方式的因素，

sentences.en: in ways that are often hurtful to others.
sentences.zh: 而这些行为往往会伤害到别人。

sentences.en: You've collaborated with the organizational psychologist Tasha Yurek, and she studies how
sentences.zh: 你曾与组织心理学家塔莎·尤里克（Tasha Eurak）合作过，她专门研究

sentences.en: self-aware people are.
sentences.zh: 人们的自我觉察能力有多高。

sentences.en: So how self-aware are people, I mean, relative to how self-aware they think they are?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们的自我觉察度到底有多高？我是说，相对于他们自己认为的自我觉察度而言？

sentences.en: Yeah, not very self-aware.
sentences.zh: 是的，自我觉察度其实不高。

sentences.en: So she has, not at all, there's a huge gap.
sentences.zh: 所以她发现——完全没有，这里面有巨大的差距。

sentences.en: So she has found that 95% of people believe that they're self-aware.
sentences.zh: 她发现95%的人都认为自己很有自我觉察能力。

sentences.en: You know, we have a good sense of our strengths and how we're perceived.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们对自己长处以及别人如何看待我们有着很好的感知。

sentences.en: However, she has found that only 10 to 15% of people actually are self-aware.
sentences.zh: 然而，她发现只有10%到15%的人真正具备自我觉察能力。

sentences.en: And so 80% of us are fooling ourselves on any given day about, you know, what people think
sentences.zh: 因此，在任何特定的一天里，我们当中有80%的人都在自我欺骗，关于

sentences.en: of us.
sentences.zh: 别人是如何看待我们的。

sentences.en: And we tend to bias it all in the positive direction.
sentences.zh: 而且我们往往会把这种偏差全部导向积极的方向。

sentences.en: Marshall Goldsmith, who coaches a lot of leaders, and he talks about this idea of we like to play
sentences.zh: 马歇尔·戈德史密斯（Marshall Goldsmith）辅导过很多领导者，他谈到过这样一个概念：我们喜欢在脑海中播放

sentences.en: a highlight reel of our successes in our minds.
sentences.zh: 自己成功经历的精彩片段集锦。

sentences.en: And so we kind of anchor in on the positives and how we affect others.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们会下意识地执着于积极的方面以及我们对他人产生的影响。

sentences.en: And our blind spots are usually on the negatives and how we're affecting people.
sentences.zh: 而我们的盲区通常在于消极的方面，以及我们是如何影响他人的。

sentences.en: In harmful ways or ways that may even hurt us.
sentences.zh: 以有害的方式，或者甚至是可能伤害我们自己的方式。

sentences.en: I understand, Christine, that you once had an encounter with a friend who revealed to you
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂，我了解到你曾经遇到过一个朋友，他向你透露了

sentences.en: something about your own behavior that you were not aware of.
sentences.zh: 一些连你自己都没有意识到的关于你自身行为的事情。

sentences.en: What did he tell you about your conversational style?
sentences.zh: 他跟你说了关于你的对话风格的什么？

sentences.en: So he told me that I had a tendency to interrupt or to jump in when someone else was speaking.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，当别人在说话时，我有打断或插话的倾向。

sentences.en: And, you know, that was something that I didn't realize that I did.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这是我以前没有意识到自己会做的事情。

sentences.en: So if there was a pregnant pause in our conversation, I was happy to help him along, finish his thoughts
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们的对话中出现了意味深长的停顿，我很乐意帮他接话，帮他把想法说完

sentences.en: or insert my question.
sentences.zh: 或者插进我自己的问题。

sentences.en: And so when I got this feedback, I was really surprised.
sentences.zh: 所以当我得到这个反馈时，我真的非常惊讶。

sentences.en: And did it feel like there was any truth to it?
sentences.zh: 你当时觉得这其中有什么道理吗？

sentences.en: It did.
sentences.zh: 确实觉得有。

sentences.en: And in fact, I think the funny thing was, as he was telling me this, I was ready to jump in with the why or
sentences.zh: 事实上，我觉得有趣的是，当他告诉我这些的时候，我已经准备好抛出理由进行辩解了，

sentences.en: the defensiveness, which had him laughing and me laughing.
sentences.zh: 这让他和我都大笑起来。

sentences.en: And, you know, if there was any doubt, that was cleared up right away in the moment.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如果还有什么怀疑的话，当时就立刻烟消云散了。

sentences.en: Christine talked earlier about the educator and coach Marshall Goldsmith.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂刚才谈到了教育家兼教练马歇尔·戈德史密斯。

sentences.en: He was a pioneer in what's called 360-degree feedback.
sentences.zh: 他是所谓的“360度反馈”的先驱。

sentences.en: It's a structured system some leaders have used to solicit the opinions of a wide range of colleagues and subordinates.
sentences.zh: 这是一个结构化的系统，一些领导者用它来征求广大同事和下属的意见。

sentences.en: As it turns out, even people who teach others to overcome their blind spots have blind spots of their own.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，即使是那些教导他人克服盲区的人，自己也有盲区。

sentences.en: So he actually collected 360-degree feedback at the consulting firm he ran.
sentences.zh: 因此，他实际上在他所经营的咨询公司里收集了360度反馈。

sentences.en: And he has a reputation for being a great guy and a giver.
sentences.zh: 而且他一直以是个大好人和乐于奉献的人而闻名。

sentences.en: And so he was really upset by the fact that the feedback he got was he had a tendency to talk badly about people behind their backs.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他得到的反馈是他有在背后说别人坏话的倾向时，他真的非常沮丧。

sentences.en: And he felt terrible, but he also couldn't think of any times where he had done this.
sentences.zh: 他感觉糟透了，但也根本想不起自己曾经做过这种事。

sentences.en: And so he challenged his employees.
sentences.zh: 于是他向员工下了挑战书。

sentences.en: He said, $10 anytime you call me out on this.
sentences.zh: 他说：“只要你们任何人抓到我这样做，一次给你们10美元。”

sentences.en: On day one, he said he was down $50 by lunchtime.
sentences.zh: 第一天，他说到午饭时间他就已经输了50美元。

sentences.en: And he locked himself in his office and decided that's enough, you know, no more for today.
sentences.zh: 于是他把自己锁在办公室里，心想够了，今天到此为止，不能再这样了。

sentences.en: And then he said he improved.
sentences.zh: 然后他说他有所改善。

sentences.en: You know, it was then $30 and then $10.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，后来变成了30美元，再后来是10美元。

sentences.en: And so his point was not that we have to put a tax on our own behavior, but even the leading coaching guru that came up with 360 feedback and everything, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以他的重点并不是说我们必须对自己的行为进行经济惩罚，而是连那位想出了360度反馈等一系列方法的顶尖教练大师，

sentences.en: he wasn't aware of behaviors that he certainly wasn't proud of.
sentences.zh: 也对那些他绝对引以为耻的行为毫无察觉。

sentences.en: I mean, it was the opposite of the effect that he wanted to have.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这完全违背了他想要达到的效果。

sentences.en: And yet he was completely unaware.
sentences.zh: 然而他却全然不知。

sentences.en: He couldn't think of a time where he had done it.
sentences.zh: 他根本想不起自己曾经做过那样的事。

sentences.en: So it even showed that we need the help of others to try to uncover some of this awareness for us so that we can improve.
sentences.zh: 所以这也表明，我们需要他人的帮助来为我们揭开部分这种认知，这样我们才能有所进步。

sentences.en: The researcher Josh Misner at North Idaho College has another idea on how you can increase the amount of feedback that you get.
sentences.zh: 北爱达荷学院的研究员乔希·米斯纳（Josh Misner）对如何增加你获得的反馈量有另一个想法。

sentences.en: And his idea has now been taken and is being used by organizational psychologists.
sentences.zh: 他的这个想法现在已经被采纳，并正在被组织心理学家们所使用。

sentences.en: Tell me about the Dinner of Truth.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲“真诚晚宴”（Dinner of Truth）吧。

sentences.en: So the Dinner of Truth is that you ask a friend or a colleague out for dinner and you ask them, you know, what's one of the most annoying habits that I have?
sentences.zh: “真诚晚宴”就是你邀请一位朋友或同事出去共进晚餐，然后问他们：“你知道的，我最烦人的习惯是什么？”

sentences.en: Or what is something that I do that, you know, hurts me or you or it leads to my ineffectiveness?
sentences.zh: 或者“我有什么行为，你知道的，会伤害到我、你，或者导致我的效率低下？”

sentences.en: And ideally, you sit there and you take the feedback and you use it to move you forward.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，你坐在那里接受反馈，并利用它来推动自己前进。

sentences.en: And although people like Tasha Yurk have told me that they thought I'm not going to get real feedback from this friend, that in fact,
sentences.zh: 尽管像塔莎·尤里克这样的人曾对我说过，他们觉得我不会从这位朋友那里得到真实的反馈，但事实上，

sentences.en: they get super valuable feedback and it's a way to move them forward.
sentences.zh: 他们得到了极其宝贵的反馈，这也是推动他们前进的一种方式。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's not easy to do in the sense of a lot of people are fearful of what they might hear.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，这并不容易做到，因为很多人都害怕听到他们可能会听到的话。

sentences.en: I want to spend a little time talking about how we might respond to incivility that's directed at us, how we can keep it from hijacking our bodies and our minds.
sentences.zh: 我想花点时间讨论一下，我们该如何应对针对我们的无礼言行，如何防止它劫持我们的身体和心灵。

sentences.en: As we've seen, confronting rudeness with rudeness doesn't seem like a very good solution.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所见，用粗鲁来回应粗鲁似乎并不是一个很好的解决方案。

sentences.en: Avoiding the perpetrator of rudeness often doesn't work very well.
sentences.zh: 避开粗鲁的施加者通常也没有什么好效果。

sentences.en: You say that one alternative is to change your own frame and to focus on the future.
sentences.zh: 你说过，另一种选择是改变你自己的心态并把焦点放在未来。

sentences.en: What do you mean by this?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's important that you control what you can control.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为控制你能控制的东西是很重要的。

sentences.en: And usually that means just yourself.
sentences.zh: 而通常这意味着仅仅控制你自己。

sentences.en: And the research shows we found that the one antidote to incivility is a sense of thriving, like a sense of feeling like you're moving forward.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，我们发现对抗无礼的唯一解药是一种蓬勃发展的感觉，比如那种感觉自己正在不断前进的感觉。

sentences.en: And so it's about getting unstuck.
sentences.zh: 所以这关乎于摆脱困境。

sentences.en: And for a lot of people, it's focusing on taking care of themselves, like, for example, exercising or something like that.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这专注于照顾好自己，比如，锻炼身体或诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: What you want to do is you want to do something that builds hope, that helps you focus on moving forward in a positive way, not getting dragged down about your paSt.
sentences.zh: 你想做的是做一些能建立希望的事情，这有助于你专注于以积极的方式向前迈进，而不是被你的过去拖垮。

sentences.en: The other aspect is a sense of vitality or energy.
sentences.zh: 另一个方面是活力感或能量感。

sentences.en: And so there are lots of ways to potentially achieve this.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多方法可以潜在地实现这一点。

sentences.en: It could be activities like getting involved in your community, coaching, volunteering, you know, choosing something that makes you feel smarter, stronger or more interesting,
sentences.zh: 它可以是参与社区活动、当教练、做志愿者等活动，你知道的，选择一些能让你感觉更聪明、更强大或更有趣的事情，

sentences.en: that really clears your mind or feeds your soul.
sentences.zh: 那些真正能让你头脑清醒或滋养你心灵的事情。

sentences.en: And we talked about a lot about incivility as a virus.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论了很多关于把无礼视为一种病毒的话题。

sentences.en: And your defense really depends to a large extent on your ability to manage your energy.
sentences.zh: 而你的防御在很大程度上确实取决于你管理精力的能力。

sentences.en: And my research suggests that many of the factors that help prevent illness, like good nutrition, sleep, stress management, can also help ward off incivility's noxious effects.
sentences.zh: 我的研究表明，许多有助于预防疾病的因素，如良好的营养、睡眠、压力管理，也可以帮助抵御无礼带来的有害影响。

sentences.en: So in some ways, to stick with the disease analogy, what I think I hear you say is if you're confronted by a virus, yes, you can go looking for the antidote to the virus.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，为了延续疾病这个类比，我认为我听到你所说的是，如果你遇到了一种病毒，是的，你可以去找这种病毒的解药。

sentences.en: But perhaps the better solution is just to have a stronger immune system.
sentences.zh: 但也许更好的解决方案只是拥有一个更强大的免疫系统。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这完全正确。

sentences.en: And there are ways that we can do that, including even, you know, building positive relationships inside or outside of work.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多方法可以做到这一点，甚至包括在工作内部或外部建立积极的关系。

sentences.en: Or if this happens to you at work, we encourage people to focus on thriving outside of work, you know, because by doing things that make you feel good outside of the workplace,
sentences.zh: 或者如果这种事在工作中发生在你身上，我们鼓励人们专注于工作之外的蓬勃发展，你知道的，因为通过做那些让你在工作场所以外感觉良好的事情，

sentences.en: you actually bring a stronger, more resilient self inside the workplace.
sentences.zh: 你实际上会把一个更强大、更有韧性的自我带入工作场所。

sentences.en: So I think that's helpful.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这很有帮助。

sentences.en: I understand that you're working with nurses to teach them strategies to thrive.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，你正在与护士们合作，教导她们蓬勃发展的策略。

sentences.en: Many, many nurses report, you know, dealing with a significant amount of incivility and rudeness in the workplace, especially perhaps during the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 许许多多的护士都报告说，她们在工作场所中应对着大量的无礼和粗鲁对待，特别是在2019冠状病毒病大流行期间。

sentences.en: There have been Asian-American nurses who've been attacked by patients about, you know, quote,

sentences.en: So one of the things that we're coaching them on that we've seen evidence and experiments that by what they call self-distancing,
sentences.zh: 所以我们对她们进行指导的内容之一，也是我们在证据和实验中看到的事情，就是通过他们所说的自我疏离（self-distancing），

sentences.en: so this idea of kind of pulling back out of the moment.

sentences.en: And it's almost like, you know, asking someone to step out and watch the scene as a movie unfolding.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是，你知道的，要求某人退后一步，像看一场正在展开的电影一样观看这个场景。

sentences.en: So trying to take a step back from the event and trying to get a better and bigger picture perspective on it.
sentences.zh: 所以要试图从事件中退后一步，并试图从中获得更好、更大局观的视角。

sentences.en: So, for example, one way you can do this is ask, okay, in five years, what kind of effect is this going to have on you?

sentences.en: So we found that self-distancing makes people more objective and less emotionally involved in the encounter.
sentences.zh: 因此我们发现，自我疏离能使人们更加客观，并在冲突中减少情绪投入。

sentences.en: And this can help individuals find better solutions in the moment and moving forward.

sentences.en: So if they have the capability to distance themselves from the stressor, let's say this rude encounter, they're able to, let's say, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果她们有能力让自己与压力源（比方说这次无礼的遭遇）保持距离，她们就能，比方说，你知道的，

sentences.en: serve the patient better in the moment or come back to the patient more quickly, you know, without, you know,

sentences.en: kind of taking it out on them or just being really wrapped up in what to make of the situation.
sentences.zh: 把气撒在他们身上，或者只是深深地纠结于如何看待这种情况。

sentences.en: We talked earlier about how when you've experienced incivility, you've often found it hard to set it aside and to basically focus on other things.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到过，当你经历无礼对待时，你经常会发现很难将其抛在一边，并且基本上专注于其他事情。

sentences.en: In some ways, incivility and rudeness can hijack the mind and make it very difficult to focus on other things.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，无礼和粗鲁会劫持大脑，使人很难专注于其他事情。

sentences.en: And so unsurprisingly, people who experience rudeness end up, you know, perseverating on the thing that happened, on the rude thing that happened, on the, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以毫不奇怪，经历过粗鲁对待的人最终会，你知道的，喋喋不休地纠结于发生的事情、发生的粗鲁事情、你知道的，

sentences.en: the rude thing that was said to them.

sentences.en: And partly I think what you're suggesting is actually so hard because what you're saying is that that kind of perseveration, in fact, is not useful.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我认为你的建议之所以如此艰难，是因为你在说这种喋喋不休的纠结实际上是没有用的。

sentences.en: In fact, it's not helpful.

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it is extremely challenging to get that advice, but it leads to a lot better results.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为接受这个建议极具挑战性，但它能带来好得多的结果。

sentences.en: And in the case of nurses, you know, when patient safety is at risk, I think it's imperative that they find coping strategies so that they can attend to people, you know,
sentences.zh: 就护士而言，你知道的，当患者的安全处于危险之中时，我认为她们必须找到应对策略，以便她们能够照顾人们，你知道的，

sentences.en: in a way that doesn't take them off track, especially for long periods of time.
sentences.zh: 以一种不会让她们偏离正轨的方式，尤其是不会持续很长时间。

sentences.en: So we're trying to find interventions or things that help them not only cope with it, but recover quickly and move them forward.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正试图寻找干预措施或能够帮助她们的事情，不仅帮助她们应对，还能让她们迅速恢复并推动她们向前发展。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: I also think that that idea of thriving is really crucial for them because they've been under such challenging circumstances and strain for a long time that it's really important that they take care of themselves.
sentences.zh: 我也认为这种蓬勃发展的理念对她们来说至关重要，因为她们长期处于如此具有挑战性的环境和压力之下，照顾好自己真的非常重要。

sentences.en: You know, just coming in as physically ready as possible because, you know,

sentences.en: it's going to help them be able to regulate and respond best to anything that they may deal with that day.

sentences.en: I'm wondering if people push back on you when you give them this advice, because I suspect that many people who have experienced incivility, you know,

sentences.en: seek justice more than anything else.

sentences.en: They actually want they want the wrong door to make amends.

sentences.en: And you're telling them the best way to deal with this really is to not pay attention to it, to move on with your day,
sentences.zh: 而你却告诉他们，处理这件事的最好方法其实是不要理会它，继续过好你的一天，

sentences.en: to try and find other things in your life that you're engaged with that make you happy.
sentences.zh: 去试着寻找你生活中能让你感到快乐的其他参与其中的事情。

sentences.en: Do people respond to that advice well, Christine?

sentences.zh: 你知道的，总的来说，我认为他们反应不错。

sentences.zh: 美好之处在于，你是在押注于自己，而不是押注于别人的改变。

sentences.en: And the vast majority of these situations at work, even if they told the organization, the organization acted on that, which is rare, you know,

sentences.en: And so really what you're asking them is to focus on themselves and bet on themselves and their future.

sentences.en: And at least for myself, like, I like that message because, you know, that gives me some power in an otherwise really disempowering situation.
sentences.zh: 至少对我自己而言，我很喜欢这个信息，因为，你知道的，这在原本会让人感到极其无力的局面中赋予了我一些力量。

sentences.en: I want to look at some complexities when it comes to incivility.
sentences.zh: 我想探讨一下涉及无礼行为时的一些复杂性。

sentences.en: You've written, what matters is not whether people actually were disrespected or treated insensitively, but whether they felt disrespected.
sentences.zh: 你写过，重要的不是人们是否真的受到了不尊重或不敏感的对待，而是他们是否感到了不尊重。

sentences.en: Incivility is in the eyes of the recipient.
sentences.zh: 无礼存在于接受者的眼中。

sentences.en: Now, I can see the virtue of taking people's concerns about incivility seriously, but I can also see some people saying, hang on a minute,
sentences.zh: 现在我能理解认真对待人们对不礼貌行为的担忧有其价值，但我也可以看到有人会说，等等，

sentences.en: if each person can decide for themselves what is rude and what is not rude, how do we come to a shared understanding of incivility?

sentences.en: I mean, so someone who's from a very polite culture, you know, let's say from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，来自非常礼貌文化的人，比如说，来自美国

sentences.zh: 南部的人来到纽约市这样的地方，可能会说，你知道的，这镇上的每个人真的很粗鲁。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's what makes it really tricky.
sentences.zh: 是的，这正是让事情变得非常棘手的原因。

sentences.en: And that's why providing information to people about how things are affecting you, at least if that's someone you work with regularly, is helpful.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么向人们提供关于事情如何影响你的信息，至少如果是与你经常共事的人，会很有帮助。

sentences.en: But, I mean, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，美国

sentences.zh: 所以我想这就是让它变得如此具有挑战性的原因。

sentences.en: or International Monetary Fund, where they have employees from 183 countries, I mean, that makes it really tough to come up with norms for communicating or how we treat each other.
sentences.zh: 所以，不久前，我偶然看到了一段视频，记录了一起发生在坦帕和亚特兰大之间的达美航空航班上的事件。

sentences.en: So, some time ago, I came by this clip of an incident that took place on a Delta Airlines flight between Tampa and Atlanta.

sentences.en: It started when the woman was told she'd have to wait for the beverage cart to move before she could take her seat.

sentences.en: And then it quickly escalated into a fight about whether to wear face masks.
sentences.zh: 很快，双方开始互相辱骂，最后，那个女人挥拳打了过去。

sentences.en: Soon, insults were flying back and forth and eventually, the woman threw a punch.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜，这段视频让我印象深刻的是，双方似乎都觉得他们是不礼貌行为的受害者。

sentences.en: What I find striking about this clip, Christine, is that both parties seem to feel like they are victims of incivility.

sentences.zh: 而如果你认为没有必要戴口罩，你可能会把我视为一个令人讨厌的、爱管闲事的人。

sentences.en: And if you think wearing a mask is not necessary, you can see me as being an obnoxious, you know, busybody.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有没有可能在许多冲突中，双方都觉得自己是不礼貌行为的受害者？

sentences.zh: 是的，因为我们可能缺乏自我意识，或者只是不同意我们所做的那些被对方认为粗鲁的事情。

sentences.en: Yes, because we may lack self-awareness or simply disagree with whatever we did that they thought was rude.
sentences.zh: 绝对存在产生错误认知的可能性。

sentences.en: There's definitely a likelihood of misperceptions.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为很多时候这种情况在电子邮件中更为常见。

sentences.en: Because over email, you don't have a person's tone or their nonverbals.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为会有很多误解，你会假设某人可能很粗鲁，

sentences.en: And so I think that there's a lot of misunderstandings where you assume that someone may be being rude

sentences.en: and may then, you know, respond with a rude email or an accusatory tone.

sentences.en: And so then it kind of gets you in a negative spiral when, in fact, some of it could have stemmed from a misunderstanding.

sentences.zh: 我认为反馈至关重要。

sentences.zh: 但我想如果在社群或家庭中，如果我们能带着这种视角来看待问题，
